articles.text:
Serena Williams And Beth Ferreira Unveil $200 Million VC Strategy Through Starfire Ventures
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 8:56 PM
Serena Williams And Beth Ferreira Unveil $200 Million VC Strategy Through Starfire Ventures
Serena Williams and Beth Ferreira have launched Starfire Ventures, an early-stage venture capital firm that plans to attract $200 million in capital for investments in technology-enabled and AI-native companies.
The New York-based firm will primarily invest in seed through Series A rounds, with selective participation in later-stage opportunities. Its target areas include vertical AI, business-to-business technology, and consumer businesses addressing significant but underserved needs.
Starfire’s investment strategy centers on companies that can expand access to health and wellness, education and knowledge, financial management, and consumer experiences. The firm is also interested in infrastructure that improves affordability and access, particularly in industries with more than $1 trillion of potential market value.
Within the experience economy, Starfire plans to evaluate new retail models, stadium technologies, entertainment platforms, interactive products, and other tools that increase access to or improve live and real-world experiences.
The new firm builds on an investment partnership between Williams and Ferreira that began in 2015. Their first collaboration involved a seed investment in online education company MasterClass.
They subsequently invested together in companies including pet food brand Ollie and meal delivery company Daily Harvest. Ollie was acquired by Agrolimen in 2026, while Chobani acquired Daily Harvest in 2025.
Ferreira later became an adviser to Serena Ventures when Williams launched the investment platform. She joined Serena Ventures as a general partner in 2024.
Starfire represents the next stage of the platform Williams established through Serena Ventures, which raised an inaugural $111 million fund in 2022. The new organization combines Williams and Ferreira’s more than 30 years of collective investment experience.
The pair have deployed hundreds of millions of venture capital dollars across their careers. Starfire is intended to pair that investment background with operating expertise, corporate relationships, and an international network that can help portfolio companies develop beyond their initial financing rounds.
The firm said it will evaluate not only the attractiveness of a company’s idea but also the commitment and capabilities of the founding team. This approach reflects Williams and Ferreira’s experience investing across multiple market cycles, when changes in financing conditions placed different demands on company leaders.
Starfire also plans to support founders beyond the initial capital investment. Potential assistance could include access to commercial partners, strategic guidance, hiring networks, brand development, follow-on financing relationships, and international connections.
The firm’s stated focus on critical and underserved problems suggests that it will look for businesses able to pair substantial commercial opportunities with broader access or participation. Examples could include technology that lowers costs, reaches overlooked customers, or creates new ways for people to use essential services.

Attorney General Mike Hilgers announces $183.5 Million multistate settlement with Rent-to-Own finance company Acima Digital, LLC
Courtesy Photo
November 15th, 2026 | Nebraska Attorney General’s Office
Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. The settlement includes $43 million in consumer restitution, $10.5 million to participating states, and $130 million in lease balance reductions. Nebraska will receive more than $292,608.42 in restitution and $593,465.05 in lease forgiveness for Nebraska consumers.
Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

African startups raise $183 million in October
By AfricanManager

African startups raised a total of $183 million in October 2026 through 34 funding deals worth at least $100,000 each, according to the monthly report published on November 5 by investment tracking platform Africa: The Big Deal.
The amount represents a 24% decline compared with September and stands 29% below the average monthly funding of $259 million recorded over the past 12 months.
The slowdown was even more pronounced year-on-year. Funding fell by 58% from the $435 million raised by African startups in October 2025. The number of announced transactions also declined, with 34 deals recorded in October, against a monthly average of 43 over the past year.
Equity financing accounts for 60% of October funding
Equity investments dominated fundraising activity, accounting for $110 million, or 60% of the total raised during the month.
Debt financing amounted to $71 million, representing 39% of total funding, while grants accounted for approximately $2 million.
The two largest transactions each reached $40 million and were concluded outside Africa’s four leading startup funding markets: Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa.
In Morocco, health tech company ABA Life secured a $40 million investment agreement with pan-African investment fund Admaius Capital Partners.
Founded in 2021, the company develops solutions combining artificial intelligence, medical technologies, telemedicine and connected healthcare infrastructure. The funding will support its artificial intelligence programme for healthcare systems and facilitate its international expansion.
In Tanzania, agritech platform East Africa Foods raised nearly $40 million to expand its processing, storage and logistics capabilities, as well as its digital tools.
The company works with more than 28,000 small-scale farmers and supplies over 10,000 urban retailers. It plans to use the financing to expand into additional East African markets.
Nigeria leads African startup funding
Nigeria topped the continental ranking in October, with nine startups raising a combined $42 million, primarily through debt financing in the energy and mobility sectors.
Morocco and Tanzania followed with $40 million each, largely driven by the two major transactions involving ABA Life and East Africa Foods.
Egypt ranked fourth with $19 million, followed by Senegal with $13 million.
A notable shift in funding distribution was also recorded. Startups based in Africa’s four largest funding markets attracted just 46% of total capital raised in October, their lowest monthly share since November 2022.

[Crypto Dealbook] November funding reaches $181 million; Index Industries leads weekly deals
November crypto venture funding totals $181 million across 21 rounds. Index Industries led weekly deals with a $50 million seed round, while 30-day funding rose despite fewer rounds.
By John Kim
Published Nov 16, 2026, 7:23 AM EST
Save Share
Mentioned assets
ONDO Ondo Data: CryptoRank · TokenPost
Crypto venture funding has reached $181 million in November, with Index Industries securing the week's largest deal through a $50 million seed round. API, payments and artificial intelligence led investment focus.
November funding so far totals $181 million across 21 rounds.
The latest monthly tally covers November through November 15.
October closed with $1.85 billion raised across 52 rounds, compared with $680.50 million across 53 rounds in September.
November 9 Seva Money raised $5 million in a seed round led by Blockwall and Revent, with other investors participating. Lithium recorded a strategic investment from LitVM with the amount undisclosed. River One recorded an M&A transaction involving Securitize, also with the amount undisclosed.
November 10 Index Industries raised $50 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed, alongside other investors. Alta secured $47.50 million in a Series A led by Index Ventures, with other participants. Marble raised $11 million in a seed round led by Polychain Capital, alongside other investors.
November 12 Griffin raised $20 million in a Series B led by Octagon Partners, with other investors participating. Kailash recorded a pre-seed round led by UTXO Management with the amount undisclosed. Spout Finance received a strategic investment from Ondo Finance with the amount undisclosed.
November 13 DI recorded funding from OKX Ventures and other investors. The amount and stage were undisclosed.
Over the latest 30 days, the investment activity index fell 35.0% from the previous month. Round counts declined while total funding increased.
The period recorded 57 investment rounds, down 19.7% month over month. Total funding rose 91.2% to $2.32 billion.
The average round size was in the $3 million to $10 million range. Strategic investment was the most active funding stage, while API was the leading investment focus.
Over the past six months, API accounted for the largest investment share at 29.96%, followed by payments at 21.59%, artificial intelligence at 19.82%, RWA at 15.42% and developer tools at 13.22%.
Coinbase Ventures led investor activity over the same period with 29 deals, followed by YZi Labs (Prev. Binance Labs) with 28, a16z Frontier and SBI Holdings with 11 each, Circle with 10, and Amber Group and Animoca Brands with 9 each.

Rapidly growing Toronto AI software company Blue J Legal Inc. has secured a nine-figure financing for the second straight year as it prepares to offer agentic products to its clientele of tax specialists.
The University of Toronto spinout led by tax law professor Benjamin Alarie has raised a US$176-million financing led by Baltimore-based JMI Equity. U.S. financiers Oak HC/FT and Sapphire Ventures, which co-led a US$122-million investment into Blue J last year, are participating, as well as past backer Intrepid Growth Partners, a Canadian AI-focused investor. The deal, set to be announced Tuesday, values Blue J at US$700-million.
Nearly US$100-million will go to buy shares from employees and early investors. Blue J plans to use its $80-million in proceeds to commercialize its nascent agent product and expand in the U.K. – its third market after the U.S. and Canada – and globally.
Blue J’s main clients are tax accountants, though it also sells to tax lawyers, making it one of several companies bringing AI-driven products to law firms to hasten the automation of often tedious, time-consuming work .
Mr. Alarie, a past associate dean of U of T’s faculty of law, founded Blue J in 2015 with fellow professors Albert Yoon and Anthony Niblett. They worked to develop AI software that would help lawyers and accountants speed up the process of researching complex taxation matters, powered by predictive analytics software. Blue J raised venture capital and generated modest sales.
Then in late 2022 OpenAI launched ChatGPT, the AI chatbot that answered text questions in seconds. Mr. Alarie realized Blue J could fold generative AI capabilities into its product to answer far more tax-research questions. “The technology wasn’t really there to allow us to create a system that could answer any arbitrary tax research question – until we saw the promise of LLMs,” he said.
Blue J rebuilt its product incorporating OpenAI’s large language models, relaunching it in mid-2023. The updated version produced answers in about 90 seconds, but they were wrong about half of the time, a by-product of the quirky tendency of LLMs to generate incorrect information.
The Toronto company set about refining its product, in part by licensing data from Tax Notes, a leading publisher of tax views and commentary, and benefiting from improvements to successive releases of LLMs. Many of its answers come from content licensed by several tax data and information providers, some in exclusive deals.
By the end of 2024, Blue J could produce answers within 10 seconds that were 95-per-cent-plus accurate and its users could have technical back-and-forth conversations about complex tax matters with the program. Some companies found users could save two hours a week each using Blue J, whose individual plans start at US$1,498 a year.
Mr. Alarie said error rates have come down by about 80 per cent this year as measured by “down votes” from users in response to its generated answers, which now occur 0.05 per cent of the time. “We can now confidently deliver an answer to just about any tax research question,” Mr. Alarie said.
Blue J’s increasing speed and accuracy spurred interest, and the number of client firms mushroomed from less than 100 three years ago to more than 1,000 at the end of 2024 and 4,000 a year later. It now serves more than 6,500 firms. Blue J’s annual recurring revenue has expanded by 165

Blue J Announces $176M in Funding at $700M Valuation to Scale AI Tax Research Agent
By James Dargan · 12 November 2026 · 1 min read
Toronto-based Blue J, which builds AI software for tax research, has secured US$176 million in a round led by Baltimore’s JMI Equity, valuing the company at US$700 million. Existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures and Intrepid Growth Partners also took part.
Nearly US$100 million will go towards buying shares from employees and early investors, with the remaining US$80 million funding the commercialisation of Blue J’s new agent product and expansion into the UK, its third market after the US and Canada.
Founded in 2015 by University of Toronto law professor Benjamin Alarie and two colleagues, Blue J answers complex tax questions in seconds with source citations. Alarie rebuilt the product around large language models after ChatGPT arrived in 2022, and says accuracy has risen from roughly 50% in early versions to more than 95%.
The deal comes just over a year after a US$122 million round in August 2025. Recurring revenue has since grown 165% to the mid-eight-figure range, and client firms have increased from fewer than 100 three years ago to more than 6,500.
JMI principal Jack Duane said the firm had tracked Blue J for years, heard strongly positive customer feedback and considers the product extremely difficult to replicate thanks to its proprietary data and domain expertise.

Novo Holdings-Backed Windward Bio Raises $175m in US IPO as Biotech Listings Gather Pace
November 13, 2026
|
by
Samuel Nwite
|
0
Windward Bio has raised $175 million in its US initial public offering, adding to a growing pipeline of healthcare and biotechnology companies tapping public markets as listings in other sectors face pressure from economic uncertainty.
The Basel, Switzerland-based drug developer sold approximately 10.3 million shares at $17 each, within its marketed range of $16 to $18. Its shares are scheduled to begin trading on Friday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol WWB.
The offering gives Windward fresh capital to advance its experimental antibody medicines for serious respiratory and dermatological diseases, with its lead programme targeting conditions that affect millions of patients worldwide. The company is backed by Novo Holdings, alongside other healthcare investors, and has attracted a $50 million commitment from French pharmaceutical group Sanofi.

Sanofi agreed to purchase $50 million in shares and pre-funded warrants through a private placement, providing Windward with an additional source of institutional backing as it enters the public market. The investment also gives the pharmaceutical group exposure to a biotechnology company developing treatments in areas where demand for new therapies remains significant.
Windward’s lead candidate, WIN378, is being developed for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or COPD. The antibody is designed to block a protein involved in airway inflammation, an approach intended to address an underlying biological mechanism contributing to both conditions.
The programme will be central to the company’s development strategy as it moves into the public market. However, WIN378 remains an experimental medicine, and its commercial prospects will depend on clinical results, regulatory approvals and its ability to demonstrate meaningful benefits over existing treatments.
Led by founder and chief executive Luca Santarelli, Windward has raised $310 million in equity financing from Novo Holdings and other healthcare investors, including OrbiMed, Blue Owl and RTW Investments.
Santarelli has previously built biotechnology businesses that attracted substantial acquisition interest from larger pharmaceutical companies. VectivBio, one of his earlier ventures, was acquired by Ironwood Pharmaceuticals for $1.2 billion in 2023. Pfizer acquired another company he was associated with, Therachon, in 2019 for $810 million.
That history provides Windward with a management team familiar with biotechnology development and the commercial pressures facing companies seeking to bring new medicines to market. However, previous acquisitions do not guarantee that its current drug candidates will achieve similar outcomes.
The company’s IPO also underscores the importance of specialist healthcare investors in financing drug development. Biotechnology companies often require substantial capital over several years before generating commercial revenue, as clinical trials, regulatory submissions, and manufacturing preparations result in costs well ahead of product launches.

Marrow Therapeutics Launches With $173 Million For Bone Marrow-Targeted Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:22 AM
Marrow Therapeutics Launches With $173 Million For Bone Marrow-Targeted Medicines
Marrow Therapeutics has launched with $173 million in combined Series A and Series B funding to develop genetic medicines for severe blood and bone marrow disorders.
The company’s $53 million Series A round was co-led by Scion Life Sciences and venBio. OrbiMed led a subsequent $120 million Series B financing.
All Series A investors participated in the Series B alongside RTW Investments, Surveyor Capital, Opaleye, NEXTBio Capital, Affinity Advisors, KKR, Spruce Street Capital, and Columbia Threadneedle Investments.
Scion Life Sciences founded Marrow Therapeutics, which is headquartered in Watertown, Massachusetts.
Developing A Bone Marrow-Targeting Platform
Marrow is developing engineered antibodies that target the transferrin receptor, also known as TfR1, in bone marrow.
The company’s Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate platform is designed to deliver therapeutic payloads directly to bone marrow cells. Marrow plans to use this approach across multiple hematologic and bone marrow diseases.
Transferrin receptors help cells acquire iron and are present on multiple cell types. Developing medicines that engage the receptor requires controlling where therapeutic material is delivered and minimizing unintended effects in other tissues.
Marrow’s platform is intended to use engineered antibodies to reach bone marrow while avoiding off-target effects. The company is particularly focused on addressing the risk of anemia that has limited some earlier approaches involving TfR1.
Marrow believes its in vivo delivery strategy could overcome limitations associated with existing genetic medicines, including safety concerns, complex manufacturing, and restricted patient access.
These potential advantages have not yet been established in human clinical trials. The company’s programs remain in preclinical development.
Lead Program Targets Two Blood Disorders
Marrow’s lead candidate, MAR-101, is being developed for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.
The program is currently undergoing studies required to support an investigational new drug application.
MAR-101 is designed to decrease BCL11A and reactivate the production of fetal hemoglobin. BCL11A is a regulator involved in the transition from fetal to adult hemoglobin after birth.
Increasing fetal hemoglobin has become a validated therapeutic strategy for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia. Fetal hemoglobin can reduce the effects of abnormal adult hemoglobin associated with these diseases.
Marrow intends to use one therapeutic approach for both conditions. The company refers to this strategy as a “pipeline in a product” because a single candidate could provide evidence supporting the delivery platform across more than one disease.
The program’s safety, durability, appropriate dose, and effectiveness will need to be evaluated through clinical studies.
Marrow is also developing additional programs for other blood and bone marrow disorders. The company has not disclosed detailed timelines or targets for those candidates.
